ITEM PARAGRAPHS
Poincare
had
an
especially
interesting
view
of
scientific
induction
.
Laws
,
he
said
,
are
not
direct
generalizations
of
experience
;
they
aren't
mere
summaries
of
the
points
on
the
graph
.
Rather
,
the
scientist
declares
the
law
to
be
some
interpolated
curve
that
is
more
or
less
smooth
and
so
will
miss
some
of
those
points
.
Thus
a
scientific
theory
is
not
directly
falsifiable
by
the
data
of
experience
;
instead
,
the
falsification
process
is
more
indirect
.
